The test image shows a cross-section of a corn ear (tip-on view). Key features:
- Tan/orange-brown kernels around perimeter
- White to grayish-brown mold filling the center/cob area
- Small black dots (possible pycnidia) scattered in the rotted tissue
- Rot appearing to come from inside outward

Top candidates: **Ear_rots_Diplodia** (white-gray mold + black pycnidia), **Ear_rots_Gibberella** (pink/red mold at tip), **Fusarium** (salmon-pink kernels, starburst pattern).

Let me view reference images for the top candidates.

**Analysis:**

**Test image features:**
- Cross-section (tip-on view) of a corn ear
- Perimeter kernels are tan/orange-brown, significantly rotted
- Center/cob area heavily rotted with white to grayish-brown mold
- Small black dots (pycnidia) visible throughout the rotted tissue
- Overall mummified/rotted appearance

**Comparison with references:**

- **Ear_rots_Diplodia**: Strong match — reference close-ups show exactly the same tan/orange-brown kernels covered with white-gray mold; description notes "raised black bumps (pycnidia)" which matches the black dots in the test image; the grayish-brown mold color is characteristic
- **Ear_rots_Gibberella**: No match — reference shows pink/red/reddish-brown mold, stalk and husk symptoms; test image has no pink coloration
- **Fusarium**: No match — reference shows bright yellow kernels with scattered white streaks/starburst pattern; test image has pervasive uniform rot, not scattered kernel infection

The test image clearly shows the hallmarks of Diplodia ear rot: white-to-grayish-brown mold, tan/brown kernels (not pink), and black pycnidia scattered throughout the rotted cob tissue.
